title: Extension of scalars preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category whose tensor
product is additive and which has functorial flat resolutions, and let
$\varphi\colon\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects of
$\mathcal C$. Let $s\colon P\to P'$ be a
quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes of $\mathcal R$-modules (K-flat for
$\otimes_{\mathcal R}$, [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]). Then
$\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}s$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of
$\mathcal S$-modules.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$. By [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] it is Grothendieck abelian, and [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] gives its symmetric relative tensor structure. The hypotheses of both nodes hold: $\mathcal C$ is closed symmetric monoidal, hence its tensor functors preserve colimits: if $X\otimes-\dashv[X,-]$, then for a small diagram $D$ the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(X\otimes\operatorname{colim}D,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{colim}D,[X,Y])\cong\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(D_i,[X,Y])\cong\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(X\otimes D_i,Y)$. Thus $X\otimes\operatorname{colim}D$ with the induced cocone has exactly the colimit universal property; symmetry gives the other variable. Also $\mathcal R$ is commutative. By [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] the relative tensor structure on $\mathcal A$ is closed. For a module $M$, write $[M,-]_{\mathcal R}$ for this right adjoint. For every small diagram $D$ of modules, $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M\otimes_{\mathcal R}\operatorname{colim}D,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\operatorname{colim}D,[M,N]_{\mathcal R})\cong\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(D_i,[M,N]_{\mathcal R})\cong\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M\otimes_{\mathcal R}D_i,N)$, proving preservation of colimits in that variable; the symmetry identifies the other fixed-factor tensor functor with this one. In particular they preserve the zero object and finite biproducts, and hence are additive: writing $f+g=\nabla\circ(f\oplus g)\circ\Delta$, the functor sends this to the same formula for $F(f)+F(g)$, since the biproduct injections, projections, diagonal and codiagonal are determined by their identity/zero component equations. Thus the relative tensor is additive in both variables, as required below. By [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] it has a functorial flat resolution. These are precisely the ambient hypotheses for the abstract K-flat resolution theorem used next; none asserts that $\mathcal S$ is flat over $\mathcal R$.

source.place: Sentence choosing a K-flat resolution: hypotheses in the module category, supplied by the module-category inheritance statements and def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom.

proof.text: Let $S_{\mathcal R}=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}(\mathcal S)$ be the regular $\mathcal S$-module restricted to $\mathcal R$; its action is $\mu_{\mathcal S}\circ(\varphi\otimes\mathrm{id})$ by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Write $S_{\mathcal R}[0]$ for the complex with this object in degree zero and zero elsewhere. Apply [lem-sfb-abstract-kflat-resolution] in $\mathcal A$ to obtain a K-flat complex $Q$ and a quasi-isomorphism $q:Q\to S_{\mathcal R}[0]$. The complex $Q$ is an $\mathcal R$-module complex, and no $\mathcal S$-action on $Q$ is required.

source.place: Sentence “Choose a K-flat resolution Q to S of S as an R-module.”

proof.text: For $K=P,P'$, put $a_K=q\otimes_{\mathcal R}\mathrm{id}_K:Q\otimes_{\mathcal R}K\to S_{\mathcal R}[0]\otimes_{\mathcal R}K$. Each $a_K$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the definition of K-flatness of $K$ in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], applied to the quasi-isomorphism $q$. Also $b=\mathrm{id}_Q\otimes_{\mathcal R}s$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the K-flatness of $Q$, applied to $s$. Let $t=\mathrm{id}_{S_{\mathcal R}[0]}\otimes_{\mathcal R}s$. Bifunctoriality gives $t\circ a_P=a_{P'}\circ b$: on every $(i,j)$ summand both composites are induced by $q^i\otimes_{\mathcal R}s^j$. The total tensor maps and their differentials are exactly those in the cited definition.

source.place: Last four sentences: the two applications of K-flatness, performed on s and q rather than on the cone.

proof.text:
Apply $H^n$ to this square. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology is functorial and the three maps $H^n(a_P)$, $H^n(a_{P'})$, $H^n(b)$ are invertible. The square gives the explicit equation
$$H^n(t)=H^n(a_{P'})\circ H^n(b)\circ H^n(a_P)^{-1}.$$
Its inverse is $H^n(a_P)\circ H^n(b)^{-1}\circ H^n(a_{P'})^{-1}$. Thus $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism of $\mathcal R$-module complexes, with no boundedness or termwise-flatness assumption on $P,P'$.

source.place: Conclusion of the tensor-resolution argument; cohomology square replaces the cone/acyclicity formulation.

proof.text: Let $T$ denote the termwise extension-of-scalars map $\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}s$ in $\mathcal S$-modules. There are natural identifications $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}(\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}K)=S_{\mathcal R}[0]\otimes_{\mathcal R}K$ for $K=P,P'$. Indeed, in degree $n$ both sides are the coequalizer of $\mathcal S\otimes\mathcal R\otimes K^n\rightrightarrows\mathcal S\otimes K^n$ by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] and [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. For the relative-tensor coequalizer, the right $\mathcal R$-action on $S_{\mathcal R}$ is $\mu_{\mathcal S}(\varphi\otimes\mathrm{id})\beta_{\mathcal S,\mathcal R}=\mu_{\mathcal S}(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varphi)$ by naturality of the braiding and commutativity of $\mathcal S$, exactly the extension-of-scalars balancing arrow. Both $\mathcal R$-actions on the quotient come from $\varphi$ followed by multiplication on $\mathcal S$. For the total tensor, only the summand $(0,n)$ is nonzero; its differential is $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal S}\otimes_{\mathcal R}d_K$, with sign $(-1)^0=1$ by [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Both induced maps for $s$ are induced by $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal S}\otimes s^n$. Consequently these identifications identify $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}(T)$ with $t$.

source.place: Sentence restricting scalars, made explicit by the two identical coequalizers and the degree-zero total tensor.

proof.text: Restriction $U=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}$ is exact between the two abelian module categories by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], under the closedness, additivity and colimit hypotheses already verified. The natural cohomology comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] therefore identifies $H^n(U(T))$ with $U(H^n(T))$ up to conjugation by its specified isomorphisms. The former is invertible by steps 4 and 5, so $U(H^n(T))$ is invertible. Finally $U$ reflects isomorphisms, directly from its being the identity on underlying morphisms and the module-morphism equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]: if $f\gamma_M=\gamma_N(\mathcal S\otimes f)$ has an inverse $g$ on underlying objects, multiplication by $g$ and $\mathcal S\otimes g$ gives $g\gamma_N=\gamma_M(\mathcal S\otimes g)$. Thus $g$ is $\mathcal S$-linear. Each $H^n(T)$ is an isomorphism, so $T$ is the required quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Sentence “Restriction of scalars is exact and faithful on underlying objects ... so it detects acyclicity”, here proved as detection of quasi-isomorphisms; Stacks 010N, homology.tex lemma-exact-functor, supplies the cohomology comparison through the cited node.
